==== generated/suppressed.d/finalize.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GENERATED FILE, do not edit.
set -euxo pipefail

# ---- /opt relocation ----
mkdir -p /usr/lib/opt
tmpfiles=/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/zz-opt-symlinks.conf
printf 'd /var/opt 0755 root root -\n' > "$tmpfiles"
for d in /opt/*/; do
    [ -d "$d" ] || continue
    name="$(basename "$d")"
    cp -a "$d" "/usr/lib/opt/${name}"
    esc="${name// /\\x20}"
    printf 'L+ /var/opt/%s - - - - /usr/lib/opt/%s\n' "$esc" "$esc" >> "$tmpfiles"
done
rm -rf /opt
mv /opt.bak /opt

# ---- module presets ----
apply_module_presets() {
    local scope="$1" dir="$2" flag=() f verb unit
    [ "$scope" = user ] && flag=(--global)
    for f in "$dir"/45-module-*.preset; do
        [ -f "$f" ] || continue
        while read -r verb unit; do
            case "$verb" in
                enable) systemctl "${flag[@]}" enable "$unit" ;;
                disable) systemctl "${flag[@]}" disable "$unit" ;;
                *) ;;
            esac
        done < "$f"
    done
}
apply_module_presets system /usr/lib/systemd/system-preset
apply_module_presets user /usr/lib/systemd/user-preset

# ---- /var to tmpfiles ----
# `rpm-ostree` walks /var at base compose time and writes these rules; nothing
# regenerates them for a derived layer, on any distro. So a directory this build
# leaves in /var is applied once at provisioning and never updated again by
# `bootc upgrade`. Runs last, after every hook: a directory a later step made
# would not be recorded.
var_conf=/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/zz-var-autogen.conf

# /var/cache and /var/log are cache mounts on this layer — busy, and not ours.
# /var/run is the symlink out to /run and stock systemd already declares it.
# ponytail: /var/lib/dpkg is skipped because on the deb bases it *is* the
# package database; drop it once the admindir moves to /usr/lib/sysimage/dpkg.
var_keep=(/var/cache /var/log /var/run /var/lib/dpkg)

# systemd splits a line on whitespace and unquotes it, then expands `%`
# specifiers in what is left, so both have to be written escaped.
var_escape() {
    local s=$1
    s=${s//\\/\\x5c}
    s=${s//%/%%}
    s=${s//$'\t'/\\x09}
    s=${s//$'\n'/\\x0a}
    s=${s//$'\r'/\\x0d}
    s=${s//$'\v'/\\x0b}
    s=${s//$'\f'/\\x0c}
    s=${s//\'/\\x27}
    s=${s//\"/\\x22}
    s=${s// /\\x20}
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

# Every path some tmpfiles.d file already declares, this run's own file
# included: systemd warns about a duplicate and drops one of the two, and
# reading our own back is what makes a second finalize over this image keep
# the entries whose directories the first one emptied.
declare -A var_declared=()
touch "$var_conf"
while read -r verb path _; do
    case "$verb" in '' | \#*) continue ;; esac
    [ -n "$path" ] && var_declared[$path]=1
done < <(cat /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/*.conf /etc/tmpfiles.d/*.conf 2> /dev/null)

var_prune=()
for keep in "${var_keep[@]}"; do
    var_prune+=(-path "$keep" -o)
done
unset 'var_prune[-1]'

# Pre-order, so a directory's own line lands above the lines below it.
var_remove=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r -d '' type mode owner group path; do
    esc="$(var_escape "$path")"
    # Already declared by another tmpfiles file: that is the base's own /var,
    # the lint does not flag it, and something later in the build may still
    # need it on disk — the rechunk runs `rpm-ostree`, which writes to
    # /var/tmp, and tmpfiles has never run inside a container build.
    [ -n "${var_declared[$esc]:-}" ] && continue
    var_declared[$esc]=1
    var_remove+=("$path")
    case "$type" in
        d) printf 'd %s %s %s %s -\n' "$esc" "$mode" "$owner" "$group" >> "$var_conf" ;;
        l) printf 'L+ %s - - - - %s\n' "$esc" "$(var_escape "$(readlink "$path")")" >> "$var_conf" ;;
        # A regular file: a tmpfiles rule reconstructs a directory, not a
        # file's content. Dropped, which is what bootc's own converter does.
        *) ;;
    esac
done < <(find /var -mindepth 1 -xdev \( "${var_prune[@]}" \) -prune -o -printf '%y\t%m\t%u\t%g\t%p\0')

# Only what was recorded above, deepest first since find listed parents before
# children. `rmdir` rather than `rm -rf`, so a directory still holding
# something that was skipped survives instead of taking it down too.
for ((i = ${#var_remove[@]} - 1; i >= 0; i--)); do
    path="${var_remove[i]}"
    if [ -d "$path" ] && [ ! -L "$path" ]; then
        rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty "$path"
    else
        rm -f "$path"
    fi
done
==== generated/suppressed.graph.md
# Suppressed capability graph

GENERATED FILE, do not edit.

An arrow points from a provider to what needs it, dotted for `after`,
which orders the build without requiring anything. Layers build left to
right.

```mermaid
graph LR
    base["ghcr.io/ublue-os/bazzite:stable"]
    m0["apps/browser"]
    base -->|"/usr/bin/flatpak, flatpak"| m0
```

## Capabilities

| Name | Kind | Provided by | Required by | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/usr/bin/flatpak` | file | `base` | `apps/browser` |  |
| `flatpak` | capability | `base` | `apps/browser` |  |
| `rechunking` | capability | `base` |  |  |

## Suppressed

The base already provides everything these declare, so nothing builds
them.

| Module | Provides |
|---|---|
| `apps/flatpak` | `flatpak`, `/usr/bin/flatpak` |
